rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an is deficient, and advises a worshipper praying behind the imam to recite it silently.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الله تعالى
rows.claim: In a hadith qudsi transmitted by Abu Hurayra, God divides al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise and glorification receive divine responses, worship is mutual, and the guidance petition belongs to the servant.
rows.anchor: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: Samura reports two pauses in the Prophet’s prayer, at the opening takbir and after al-Fatiha’s closing words; Imran disputed his memory, but Ubayy ibn Kaʿb affirmed that Samura had preserved it.
rows.anchor: فَحَدَّثَ سَمُرَةُ بْنُ جُنْدُبٍ، أَنَّهُ حَفِظَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم سَكْتَتَيْنِ

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that one pause was when prayer began and another after recitation, adding a clarification associating the latter with saying al-Fatiha’s final words.
rows.anchor: قُلْنَا لِقَتَادَةَ مَا هَاتَانِ السَّكْتَتَانِ قَالَ إِذَا دَخَلَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَإِذَا فَرَغَ مِنَ الْقِرَاءَةِ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the Prophet recited al-Fatiha’s closing words, he said Amin loudly enough for the first row to hear.
rows.anchor: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا تَلاَ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs followers to say Amin after the imam recites these words; when their utterance coincides with the angels’, their previous sins are forgiven.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Musa relays the Prophet’s prayer instructions: align rows, follow the imam’s takbir, bowing, and prostration; say Amin after 1:7 and praise God after the imam’s praise; the taught tahiyyat has an Ahmad transmission with two omissions.

none: The report concerns the permissibility of ruqya and does not explain or interpret 4:113.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Umar reports the Prophet’s explanation: God brought Adam’s descendants forth as two groups destined for Paradise or Fire; each is enabled to perform the matching deeds until death, which lead to that end.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم سُئِلَ عَنْهَا

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet used the verse’s concluding praise while prostrating, within a supplication that glorifies God as the best of creators.
